topic: CRISPR-Cas9 Molecular Cleavage and DNA Repair Mechanism

claims.statement: Cas9 forms a ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex with a single guide RNA (sgRNA) comprising a 20-nt spacer targeting sequence and scaffold.
claims.truthCondition: Cas9 endonuclease is catalytically inactive as apo-protein and requires crRNA:tracrRNA duplex or engineered chimeric sgRNA for structural activation
claims.simplificationBoundaries: Natural bacterial systems use separate crRNA and tracrRNA; engineered single guide RNA (sgRNA) fuses both with a tetraloop
claims.predictiveQuestion: What activates the endonuclease activity of Cas9?
claims.predictedAnswer: Binding to the single guide RNA (sgRNA) to form the functional ribonucleoprotein complex

claims.statement: Cas9 requires an initial Protospacer Adjacent Motif (PAM) 5'-NGG-3' recognition on the non-target strand before interrogating DNA sequence.
claims.truthCondition: SpCas9 specifically interrogates PAM via major and minor groove interactions using Arg1333 and Arg1335 before duplex unwinding
claims.simplificationBoundaries: SpCas9 primarily recognizes 5'-NGG-3'; non-canonical 5'-NAG-3' has ~5-10x lower affinity
claims.predictiveQuestion: Can Cas9 unwind DNA without first finding a PAM site?
claims.predictedAnswer: No, PAM recognition is the mandatory kinetic prerequisite for local DNA duplex destabilization

claims.statement: Cas9 utilizes two distinct catalytic nuclease domains: HNH cleaves the target strand, while RuvC cleaves the non-target strand.
claims.truthCondition: HNH domain active site (His840) cuts the DNA strand complementary to sgRNA; RuvC domain active site (Asp10) cuts the displaced non-target strand
claims.simplificationBoundaries: Mutation of either active site yields a nickase (Cas9n D10A or H840A); mutation of both yields dead Cas9 (dCas9)
claims.predictiveQuestion: Which domain cleaves which DNA strand?
claims.predictedAnswer: HNH cleaves the complementary guide-bound strand; RuvC cleaves the displaced non-target strand

claims.statement: Cleavage results in a blunt double-strand break located precisely 3 base pairs upstream of the PAM sequence.
claims.verifiableSource: Jinek et al. (Science 2012) & Addgene CRISPR Reference Guide
claims.truthCondition: Phosphodiester backbones of both strands are severed between nucleotide positions -3 and -4 counting upstream from the 5' PAM edge
claims.simplificationBoundaries: Trace frequencies of staggered 1-bp cleavage have been documented in vitro under high enzyme concentrations, but canonical cleavage produces blunt ends
claims.predictiveQuestion: Where does the double-strand cut occur relative to PAM?
claims.predictedAnswer: Exactly 3 base pairs upstream of the PAM motif, completely severing both DNA strands into two disconnected fragments

claims.statement: Non-Homologous End Joining (NHEJ) repairs double-strand breaks by direct ligation, frequently generating insertion or deletion (indel) mutations that disrupt reading frames.
claims.truthCondition: NHEJ can ligate cleanly, but persistent Cas9 recutting of perfect junctions eventually selects for error-prone indels that abolish the target/PAM sequence
claims.simplificationBoundaries: NHEJ is not inherently defective; the emergence of indels in CRISPR experiments is driven by iterative cleavage cycles until target sequence destruction
claims.predictiveQuestion: Why does CRISPR targeting usually result in gene knockout via NHEJ?
claims.predictedAnswer: Iterative cleavage and rejoining cycles continue until an error-prone indel creates a frameshift mutation that prevents Cas9 from rebinding

claims.statement: Homology-Directed Repair (HDR) enables precise sequence replacement when provided with an exogenous donor DNA template containing homology arms.
claims.truthCondition: HDR uses homologous flanking sequences to copy the donor sequence into the cleaved chromosomal site during S/G2 phase of the cell cycle
claims.simplificationBoundaries: HDR efficiency is generally lower (1-10%) than NHEJ (20-60%) in mammalian somatic cells without cell cycle synchronization or chemical inhibitors
claims.predictiveQuestion: What is required for precise gene insertion rather than random knockout?
claims.predictedAnswer: An exogenous donor DNA template containing homologous left and right homology arms flanking the desired sequence insert
